title: Precision Gatekeeper for Optimize recommendations: tiered gating, cohort canaries, and approval choreography
creator: Ava Cho
description: Create a robust, low-friction gatekeeper service that safely auto-applies Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization hints) while supporting tiered policy enforcement, cohort-based canaries, and clear human-in-the-loop approval choreography. This ticket covers the runtime-facing control plane, approval UX hooks, safety checks, and observable rollback triggers required by product and SRE to enable production autopilot for low-risk workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper API supports policy tiers: auto-apply, suggested (requires approval), and blocked
Canary cohorts can be defined by customer segment (small, medium, enterprise) and by route SLA tags
Dry-run mode produces a predictive simulation of cost and latency impact with >=95% fidelity vs. shadow traffic baseline
Automatic rollback triggers fire when cost savings drop below configured thresholds or when latency/quality regressions exceed SLOs
Operator approval flow integrates with Console rollouts and sends single-click approvals to on-call and PMs
Audit log entries are generated for every decision (apply/skip/rollback) and exported to the customer audit pipeline
End-to-end smoke test validating canary cohort ramp from 1% to 30% with staged metrics checks
tasks: Design gate schema and policy language for Optimize recommendations (tier, thresholds, preconditions)
Implement Gatekeeper service with REST gRPC endpoints and idempotent apply semantics
Integrate with existing rollout engine to support cohort ramping and scheduled ramps
Add dry-run simulator that replays representative traces against proposed config changes
Wire approval signals into Console: request, notify, approve/reject, escalate
Create default safe policies and a black/whitelist for risky changes
Add metric collectors for cost delta, latency P50/P95/P99, error rates, and eval-set quality metrics
Write runbooks for manual rollback and postmortem triggers
decisions: Use progressive cohort ramping (percentage-based) rather than fixed customer counts to simplify rollout orchestration
Dry-run results will be computed using shadowed inference traces and the runtime cost estimator; for initial rollout we accept up to +/-5% estimator error
Approval levels: low-risk auto-apply (no human), medium-risk requires PM+SRE approval, high-risk mandates an on-call sign-off
Rollback window default is 60 minutes after ramp start; can be shortened/extended per-policy
Integrate with existing audit export format to avoid schema churn in Compliance pipelines
tradeoffs: Conservative gates reduce risk but delay cost savings — chosen default leans safety-first for first 8 weeks
Cohort segmentation by route and customer tier increases complexity in rules but yields more precise risk control
Shadow/dry-run fidelity requires compute overhead; we'll restrict expensive sims to proposals estimated to save >=5%
Tighter automatic rollback thresholds could produce noisy reverts; we mitigate with multi-metric confirmation (cost + latency + eval quality)
testing_plan: Unit tests for Gatekeeper policy evaluation and idempotent apply path
Integration tests that run full canary ramps in a staging cluster using synthetic traffic
Golden-run dry-run comparisons against recorded inference traces from 10 representative customers
Chaos tests: inject increased latency and errors during canary ramps to verify rollback behavior
Security review and pen-test for approval endpoints and audit export
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboard: Gatekeeper -> Active Ramps (per-policy, per-cohort) with cost delta and latency overlays
Alert: Canary rollback threshold breached (P1) — channels: #sre-alerts, on-call page
Alert: Dry-run fidelity drift > 10% across recent proposals
Metric: percentage of proposals auto-applied vs. approved vs. rejected
Audit export: every decision written to audit.log with request_id and operator_id
rollout_plan: Week 0: Internal alpha - run Gatekeeper in dry-run against internal accounts only
Week 1: Expand to small customers with auto-apply policy and strict monitoring
Week 3: Enable medium customers with medium-risk gate that requires PM+SRE approval
Week 5: Open low-friction autopilot for a curated subset of enterprise customers with explicit opt-in
Backout plan: immediate full rollback flag in Console that aborts ongoing ramps and reverts configs
Post-rollout: 4-week evaluation window where default policies remain conservative and SRE reviews every rollback
